result.title: Label-Free Localization and Test-Time Suppression of CLIP's Typographic Circuits
result.summary: CLIP-based Vision-Language Models have become cornerstones of modern multimodal systems. The cross-modal contrastive objective equips the CLIP vision encoder to both see objects and read text. These two abilities induce an entanglement between the encoding of lexical and semantic shapes, creating a distinctive vulnerability to typographic attacks, in which rendered text overrides an image's semantic content with its literal meaning. The black-box nature of these encoders has prevented a mechanistic interpretation of such entanglement. We introduce a head-decomposed Sparse Dictionary Learning (SDL) architecture that, by design, decomposes individual attention heads into interpretable, head-specific latents. Based on this inductive disentanglement, we re-purpose Clarity Score and propose normalized Text Attribution Score, which are both label-free, to identify attention heads that carry typographic information. As a causal validation of successful circuit separation, we perform a mechanistic intervention that reweighs attention away from the patch tokens in the identified lexical heads at test-time. Experiments show that the intervention effectively recovers object classification under typographic attack and, across five CLIP variants and four typographic benchmarks, achieves up to 46.9% improvement while incurring up to 1% accuracy loss in general image perception, outperforming prior supervised and training-free methods. Expanding on the mechanistic intervention, we propose a test-time adaptive attention head routing to further reduce the impact on performance at matched robustness, pushing beyond the Pareto frontier of current robustness-perception tradeoff.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出按注意力头分解的稀疏字典学习结构，用无标签的 Clarity Score 与归一化 Text Attribution Score 定位 CLIP 中承载排版文字信息的注意力头，并通过测试时重加权及自适应头路由抑制排版攻击。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉编码器内部词形与语义表征的纠缠、无标签证据定位和因果性测试时干预，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与 latent 状态控制提供借鉴，值得核查其头级潜变量是否可迁移到推理任务。
